issue.title: Keep 💡 source badges break under Jump to link (Ctrl+L): make them title-free without losing provenance

task_type_fields.impact: Ctrl+L on every 💡 badge opens a corrupted Keep URL; the title cannot simply be dropped because parse_source_url only accepts the exact titled shape and migrate-tasks depends on it for import history.
task_type_fields.repro: Write a Keep source badge as [💡](https://keep.google.com/u/0/#NOTE/ID "Open in Google Keep"), then trigger mrj-jump-to-link 0.6.2 (Ctrl+L) in editing mode: its regex /\[[^[\]]+?\]\(.+?:\/\/.+?\)/g captures through the first ), so window.open receives 'URL "title"' and the browser encodes it as URL%20%22Open%20in%20Google%20Keep%22. Verified in the scratch-vault probe for 📅/📍/💡 links; untitled badges open cleanly.

issue.creation_reason: Approved gcal badge plan leaves Keep badges titled, so the same Ctrl+L URL corruption still breaks Keep links; filing the separate provenance-safe fix.

fields.description:
## Bug

- **Location:** `src/native/gkeep/render.rs::parse_source_url`, `src/native/gkeep/migrate_tasks.rs`, `bob gkeep migrate-tasks --help`

Titled Keep badges (`[💡](https://keep.google.com/u/0/#NOTE/ID "Open in Google Keep")`) break the same way as the gcal badges fixed in plan:202611/gcal_badge_link_titles.md. The Jump to link plugin (mrj-jump-to-link 0.6.2, Ctrl+L) finds external links with `/\[[^[\]]+?\]\(.+?:\/\/.+?\)/g` and calls `window.open(captured)`; the capture runs to the first `)`, folding the `"title"` into the URL, which the browser encodes as `%20%22Open%20in%20Google%20Keep%22`.

Verified in the scratch-vault probe: titled 📅, 📍, and 💡 links opened `URL "title"`, while an untitled 📅 opened cleanly. Plain Obsidian handles titles, so only naive parsers break.

They need a separate change because the title is gkeep's provenance marker: `parse_source_url` accepts only the exact titled shape so ordinary links never create import history, `migrate_tasks.rs` writes and parses the titled form, and the help text documents it. Related (not duplicate): bob-cli-e1 covers link titles leaking into minted block IDs.

payload.description: Both involve Markdown link titles leaking into derived outputs; e1 mints block IDs from link text while this bead keeps Ctrl+L URLs clean without losing Keep provenance
